I talked with Derek about a couple of the questions that I had in the review. Below were his requests on how this should work:
* When the application is first starting, the GPIO values in the Chassis class should be set to undefined, not 0. When you later add code that takes action based on those Chassis GPIO values, it should not take action if the value is undefined.
* When the application is first starting, and Gpio::getPreviousValue() is undefined, then the application should just use Gpio::getValue() as the value. It will just do the deglitching/two in a row logic for subsequent cycles when both getValue() and getPreviousValue() are defined. This will have the following results:
  * The first time a GPIO is successfully read, that value will be used as the value in the Chassis class.
  * If the first GPIO read fails, but the GPIO has a default value, then that default value will be used as the value in the Chassis class.
  * Thus, the Chassis class will not need to know if the GPIO has a default value, and the default value will be used.

If findLine() succeeds, don't we want to also do a requestRead() and a getValue()? Is there a reason the GPIO has to wait until the next monitor() cycle?

If findLine() fails, then we want to skip to the next GPIO right?
Done

Since this method does the release(), would it make sense to have it also do the requestRead()?

Seems like they should be in the same method to make it easier to make sure both happen. That would also make monitor() simpler.

Same comment for the other read*Value() methods.

It seems like a lot of the code in the three read*Value() methods is very similar.

Could you implement some common code, like readGPIOValue(Gpio& gpio, int& currentValue) that has most of these lines? Then readFaultLatchedValue() could just call readGPIOValue(gpio, faultLatchedValue)?

It probably depends on what ends up going into the "// handle gpio change" blocks. Just trying to reduce copy/paste.
I can do that
Done

My understanding in reading the Gpio class is that the first time the GPIO is read, getPreviousValue() is going to throw an exception because it does not have a value (undefined). That is not a problem and makes sense.

Is your intention for the exception to be caught below and ignored? So on the first monitor() cycle, presenceGPIOValue will not get set? If so, it might be helpful to add a comment indicating that.

If that is not your intention, then you need to put a try/catch around the call to getPreviousValue() and then decide how you want to handle the previous value being undefined in your logic on line 112.
Done
Just curious - what will go here in the future?
I plan making a handler method for the presence changes, and call that handler here.

This name is a little confusing, since it sounds like it would return a GPIO object rather than a GPIO value.

I'm guessing the reason it isn't called getPresence() is because there is another source of presence via the path?

What is the planned API when presence via path is implemented? It can't be called getPresencePath(), since that already returns the path vs. the presence based on the path.

Also, who will own the logic of determining what the "true" chassis presence is, based on ANDing or ORing those two together? Will the Chassis class own that, so the caller doesn't need to know the details?

If the Chassis class will own the logic of finding the "truth", one naming option would be something like:
* getPresenceFromGPIO()
* getPresenceFromPath()
* getPresence()

Normally the Chassis class user would call getPresence(), and it would return the "true" presence based on the other two. The other two would be called by automated tests, and they could be helpful if the Chassis class user needs more details for some reason.

Not a big deal. Just a question/suggestion.

I'm guessing the reason it isn't called getPresence() is because there is another source of presence via the path? - yes. 

What is the planned API when presence via path is implemented?
I believe it would be good to have a over arching presence value (source of truth), and then the gpio value separate. Presence path should only be checked when the gpio changes values so a method to get the value but not store it would be my preference. 

who will own the logic of determining what the "true" chassis presence is, based on ANDing or ORing those two together?

Chassis should own the presence. What would you think of
- getPresenceGPIOValue()
- getPresenceFromPath()
- getPresenceValue()
That sounds fine

Different naming style due to the presence path option affecting how chassis presence will be determined. Planning on another variable for the actual presence state.

You are not specifying initial values for these. It likely defaults to 0, but if that is what you want it would be more clear to specify {0}.

However, should these actually be std::optional<int> like in the Gpio class? That way you can tell the difference between "I don't know the value" and "I read a 0 value".

This is related to my comment on setting these values in the .cpp file. If these values rely on Gpio::getPreviousValue(), that is not going to be defined in the first monitor cycle. Also, if an attempt to find a line or request it fails, then it won't have a value in the first monitor cycle.

If other code is going to call getFaultLatched(), should that code get a 0 in these cases? Or should it know that the value is currently undefined?
